title: Step 1-1 — Dense 1B Data-Loader Study
setup: Dense 1B; exact repeated 1B-token document pool; sequence length 4096; default OLMo sequence reshuffling compared with dynamic document repacking and a fixed epoch-1 sequence/batch permutation; the first DR probe used LR1e-3/WD0.1 and neighboring LR/WD coordinates are being audited; BS512 and BS1024 additions use four 8-GPU nodes with rank microbatch eight sequences.
selection: The existing OLMo-core baseline is shown only for BS64 through BS1024. E1 is common to all three data-order modes, and an E2 branch may resume any exact LR/WD-matched E1 pre-decay checkpoint. BS1024 DR E2 shows a large LR effect: LR5e-4/WD0.333 reached CE3.997 versus LR1e-3/WD0.333 CE4.128, while WD0.1 and WD0.333 are essentially tied at LR5e-4. The remaining lower-LR and higher-WD boundaries are therefore audited before selecting E4. Later endpoints must resume the exact same-coordinate predecessor. Dynamic repacking preserves the original E1 packing and begins repacking at E2; fixed order reuses the exact default E1 sequence permutation and batch membership forever.

selectionPolicy.learningRate: Initial probe 1e-3; DR coordinate descent compares 5e-4 and, when the lower boundary wins materially, 2.5e-4.
selectionPolicy.dynamicRepackingDirection: At BS1024 E2, LR5e-4 materially beats LR1e-3 while WD0.1 and WD0.333 are nearly tied. Close the LR2.5e-4 and LR5e-4/WD1.0 boundaries before selecting E4.
selectionPolicy.fixedOrderDirection: At E2 begin at WD0.333 and expand upward if needed, targeting Fixed > ordinary > DR; from the selected E2 coordinate onward test only equal or higher WD.
